messages:
maria-support: FYI customer 'AcmePayments' on Private (VPC peered via Direct Connect eu-west-1) reporting intermittent 503s to the Redwood control plane since they cut over the new DX circuit around 12:25 UTC. They see spikes ~12:30 and 12:40. They suspect a peering change but also report TLS failures from app logs. Attaching brief outputs below.
jordan-sre: Can you paste the BGP show + a minimal tcpdump/traceroute from their VPC? 503 could be our backend returning 503 or a middlebox killing TLS. Also confirm whether this affects only control plane (api) or data plane (dedicated endpoints).
maria-support: short snippets from customer (sanitized):
```
# show ip bgp summary (customer edge)
BGP router identifier 10.1.0.1, local AS 65050
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.2.0.2        4 65010   10234   10210        0    0    0 00:40:12       0

# tcpdump (summary) on app host
12:30:15 IP 10.3.5.10.443 > 10.4.6.20.53124: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0
12:30:16 IP 10.3.5.10.443 > 10.4.6.20.53124: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0

# curl from app -> api (fails intermittently)
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, unknown CA (??)
* SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

maria-support: Customer says their partner-peer applied an updated policy during cutover; they saw BGP resets then flaky TLS until ~12:50. They also mentioned their edge does TLS inspection/proxy for outbound HTTPS.
alex-eng-infra: Two quick observations: 1) Their BGP neighborship in the snippet shows State/PfxRcd=0 — they're not advertising prefixes to us (routes suppressed). 2) TLS inspection + active MITM proxy will break client cert validation/OCSP stapling for our control plane. If their proxy replaces cert chain or removes OCSP, the client will throw verify errors -> 503 from our auth check layer.
elena-netops: +1. If a customer performs TLS interception we need them to either 1) exempt api.redwood.internal (passthrough) so our certs are intact, or 2) install our CA (bad idea for security). Also ensure egress allowlist allows OCSP responders and CRL endpoints used by Redwood (we saw customers forget ocsp.tls.redwood and ocsp2.redwood). Without egress to OCSP you can see handshake timeouts that cascade.
devon-custeng: I repro'd from their VPC in a debug session using a namespace and a small curl test:
```
# from customer app host
curl --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.4.6.20 -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.4.6.20) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: received alert: 'handshake failure'
* Closing connection 0
* SSL: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

devon-custeng: The proxy is substituting certs. Also their partner AS changed to 65010 during cutover (we expect 65100). That explains the BGP suppression observed.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0422-78; severity P1-s1. Pager duty notified: oncall@sre.
kevin-privops: Triage checklist/next steps I recommend:
- Ask customer to temporarily disable TLS interception for api.redwood.internal (passthrough) OR allow our CN chains to pass unmodified.
- Ensure outbound egress to OCSP/CRL endpoints is allowed (tcp/443 to ocsp*.redwood-internal and to common CAs' responders).
- Restore correct BGP ASN with partner or re-establish session so prefixes are advertised (we need their /26s present in our RIB).
- As a short-lived workaround we can route their control plane traffic via our fallback peering in us-west-2 if they accept cross-region traffic for control plane only.
maria-support: Relayed the recommendations. Customer updated partner to re-enable original ASN and configured TLS passthrough for api.redwood.internal. They're also allowing ocsp.* and outbound 443 to CA responders. They're keeping us posted during 1h monitoring window.
alex-eng-infra: I can confirm we received updated BGP announcements a few minutes ago; prefixes are now showing in RIB and active paths exist. Our metrics: control-plane 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.4% over 10 min after change :thumbsup:
devon-custeng: Customer confirms they see successful 200s from their app right now and the curl test passes. Will monitor for 1hr then close.
maria-support: Great. I'll keep the incident open until the customer confirms 1h no regression and then we'll close. Thanks all. :heart:
